title: Light and shadows
examples: Teacher, why are shadows always cast when there is light?
Can you show us what happens when light passes through different materials?
Does the color of the light change the shadow?

explain.say: Light always travels in straight lines.
If light bends, it does not travel in a straight line.
Opaque objects block all the light completely.
Translucent objects let some light pass through.
Transparent objects let most light pass through clearly.
When you stand between a light and a wall, your shadow forms.

draw.text: Shadows form when light is blocked.

faq.q: Why are shadows always cast when there is light?
faq.a: Shadows are formed because an object blocks the path of light, and light travels in straight lines.
A window can be transparent if it is clean glass, but if it is dirty, it becomes translucent.
asks: What makes a window block light?

faq.q: Does the material have to be solid to make a shadow?
faq.a: Yes, the object must be opaque, meaning it must block almost all the light completely to make a dark shadow.
asks: Can something see-through make a shadow?
What kind of object makes the darkest shadow?

faq.q: How do I tell if something is translucent?
faq.a: If you shine a light through it and you can see the light but the object is blurry, it is translucent.
asks: What is the difference between translucent and transparent?
Can you show me an example of translucent?

faq.a: Shadows change length because the angle of the light source changes as the sun moves across the sky.
asks: Does the time of day affect shadows?
Why are shadows long in the morning?

facts: Light always travels in straight lines.
Transparent materials allow most light to pass through.
Shadows are formed when light hits an opaque object.

quiz.say: Which material allows most light to pass through clearly?
quiz.why: Transparent materials let most light pass through so you can see clearly.

wrong.0: The light source is what makes the light, not the material itself.
wrong.2: Opaque things block all the light, so you cannot see through them.
wrong.3: Translucent things let some light through, but they make things look blurry.

quiz.say: If you shine a torch through a sheet of tracing paper, what is the paper?
quiz.why: Tracing paper lets some light through, making the image visible but fuzzy.

wrong.1: If it were opaque, no light would pass through at all.
wrong.2: If it were transparent, you would see everything perfectly clearly.
wrong.3: This describes how light travels, not the material itself.

quiz.say: When the sun is high in the sky, your shadow is:
quiz.why: When the light source is directly overhead, the shadow cast on the ground is at its shortest.

wrong.0: Longest shadows happen when the light source is low, like sunrise.
wrong.1: Shadows are always cast by light travelling in straight lines.
wrong.2: The shadow is always there as long as the light source is shining.
